events.text: Siting work for the line commenced.

evidence.quote: Siting commenced in 1918

events.label: approval
events.text: Parliament approved building the line with standard gauge.

evidence.quote: On 3 August 1918 , the line was passed by the Parliament of Norway
The plans were passed in 1918
by 1919 , an administration for the works had been established in Kongsberg

events.text: Construction commenced between Fossan and Bratterud.

evidence.quote: Construction commenced on 2 July 1920 , between Fossan and Bratterud

events.text: Construction resumed in March after a strike.

evidence.quote: resulting in construction not being taken up until March 1921

events.label: approval
events.text: Parliament gave final approval for construction.

evidence.quote: Final approval by parliament was first made on 20 July 1921

events.text: Partial opening: trains ran from Kongsberg to Bakkerød.

evidence.quote: Trains could run the from Kongsberg to Bakkerød from 15 November 1924
the first trains started running in 1924
the to Kjærre from 1 December 1925
to Rødberg from 1 December 1926

events.text: Official opening of the line by King Haakon VII.

evidence.quote: The official opening took place on 19 November 1927 by King Haakon VII
the line was officially opened in 1927

events.label: rationalisation
events.text: Operations rationalised; station masters replaced by clerks at fifteen stations.

evidence.quote: In 1932 , the operations were rationalized

events.label: service_change
events.text: Last scheduled steam locomotive service ran on the line.

evidence.quote: NSB used steam power for freight trains until 1970 , when NSBs last scheduled steam locomotive service hauled a gravel train

events.label: closure_decision
events.text: Parliament decided to close the line, keeping Kongsberg–Rollag for freight.

evidence.quote: In 1988 , the parliament decided to close many Norwegian lines , including the Numedal Line

events.label: service_end
events.text: Last passenger train operated on the line.

evidence.quote: The last passenger train operated on 31 December 1988
The last regular train ran in 1988

events.label: closure
events.text: Line north of Rollag officially closed.

evidence.quote: the line north of Rollag was officially closed on 1 January 1989
Since 1989 , this is the furthest north the line is kept operational
In 2013 , Jernbaneverket reopened a 30km stretch between Kongsberg and Flesberg

events.text: Derailment on the line (April 2014); the entire stretch was afterwards upgraded with new sleepers

evidence.quote: Following a derailment in April 2014 , the entire stretch was upgraded with new sleepers

undated_mentions: First plans for a line through Numedal launched after 1871 (no exact date)
Diesel multiple units introduced for passenger trains in the 1930s
Service reduced considerably during World War II (steam hauling)
Trains sometimes ran only Kongsberg to Veggli in the 1950s
Discussion about closing the line started in the 1950s
Round trips reduced to three per day in the 1960s
School trains operated for a short period in the 1980s
Friends of the Numedal Line founded after the closure (no exact date)
